title: Comparison of the adhesion-preventative effect of HaemoCer PLUS and isotonic saline solution after endometriosis treatment using transvaginal sonography.
summary:
Postoperative adhesions can cause significant clinical problems. On the one hand, adhesions can cause severe symptoms such as persistent pain; on the other hand, they can affect fertility or the patency of the fallopian tubes in the small pelvis. The latter is particularly the case in patients with endometriosis.
Difficulties may also arise during any follow-up operations in an adhesion site. The duration of the operation is generally prolonged by the presence of adhesions, and the risk of complications also increases. Therefore, special attention should be paid to the prevention of adhesions during endometriosis repair surgery.
The study includes patients with planned endometriosis treatment. As a standard method of adhesion prevention, the small pelvis is rinsed with 100 ml of isotonic saline solution after endometriosis treatment, which is then left intra-abdominally.
This study will now investigate whether the effect of isotonic saline solution for adhesion prevention after endometriosis treatment is less than that of HaemoCer PLUS.
conditions: Endometriosis of rectovaginal septum and vagina

interventions.name:
The operation for complete endometriosis removal is performed according to the clinic's general treatment standards.
Intervention group: After removal of the endometriosis, HaemoCer PLUS is applied to the resulting lesions.
Control group: After removal of the endometriosis, 100 ml of 0.9% NaCl is applied to the resulting lesions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Suspicion of moderate to severe endometriosis (at least stage II endometriosis according to rASRM)
• Existing uterus
Exclusion criteria:
• Pregnant patients
• Intestinal endometriosis
• Known intolerance to starch or starch containing products
